note: National baseline. Items marked unverified_seed were written from general knowledge and are waiting for the agent or a contributor to attach a source.

who_legislates.land: State subject: land, land revenue and land records (State List entries 18 and 45). Parliament legislates on acquisition (Concurrent List entry 42) and on transfer of property and registration (Concurrent List entry 6).
who_legislates.labour: Concurrent subject (entries 22–24): Parliament and states can both legislate; states write the rules that make the national labour codes work locally.
who_legislates.capital: Mostly Union subjects: banking, companies, securities, foreign exchange, insolvency (Union List entries 43–46 and Concurrent List entry 9).
who_legislates.tax: Split by the Constitution: income and corporation tax go to the Union; stamp duty, land revenue and taxes on professions to states; property tax to municipalities under state law; GST is shared under Art. 246A.

laws.title: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act
laws.summary: Governs compulsory acquisition of land. Requires a social impact assessment and, for private and public-private projects, the consent of most affected landowners; compensation is tied to market value with a multiplier for rural land and a 100% solatium. Several states have amended it for their own projects.

laws.title: Registration Act
laws.summary: Makes registration compulsory for most transfers of immovable property; registration offices are run by states.

laws.title: Indian Stamp Act
laws.summary: Framework for stamp duty on documents. States set the rates on property sales and most other instruments, so the cost of buying land differs by state.

laws.title: Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act
laws.summary: Gives gram sabhas in Fifth Schedule areas a say over land acquisition, minor forest produce and minerals.

laws.title: Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act
laws.summary: Recognises individual and community rights of forest-dwelling communities over forest land.

laws.title: Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act
laws.summary: Requires registration of real-estate projects with a state regulator and escrow of buyers' money.

laws.title: Code on Wages
laws.summary: Sets a national floor wage and governs minimum wages, payment of wages and bonus. States notify their own minimum wages above the floor.

laws.title: Industrial Relations Code
laws.summary: Trade unions, standing orders and dispute resolution; raises the threshold for prior permission for layoffs and closures to 300 workers, which states may change.

laws.title: Code on Social Security
laws.summary: Provident fund, state insurance, maternity benefit and gratuity; extends social security to gig and platform workers.

laws.title: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code
laws.summary: Workplace safety, working hours and conditions, including for inter-state migrant workers.

laws.title: Companies Act
laws.summary: Incorporation, governance and disclosure for companies.

laws.title: Securities and Exchange Board of India Act
Foreign Exchange Management Act
laws.summary: Governs cross-border payments and foreign investment.

laws.title: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code
laws.summary: Time-bound insolvency resolution for companies and individuals.

laws.title: SARFAESI Act
laws.summary: Lets secured lenders enforce security without going to court.

laws.title: Central Goods and Services Tax Act
laws.summary: A single tax on goods and services shared between the Union and states. From 22 September 2025 most items fall in two slabs, 5% and 18%, with a 40% rate for a short list of goods.

laws.title: Income-tax Act
laws.summary: Replaces the Income-tax Act, 1961 from 1 April 2026. Under the default new regime, resident individuals with taxable income up to ₹12 lakh pay no tax because of the rebate.

gst_slabs_pct.note: Plus nil-rated items and special rates for precious metals.

professional_tax_cap_inr_per_year.note: Constitutional cap on what any state can levy (Art. 276).

corporate_tax_concessional_pct.note: Base rate for domestic companies opting for s. 115BAA-type regime, before surcharge and cess.
